slides.texte_overlay:
How to become ridiculously
social at a new job
Learn ten names in your first week. Write them down after meetings if you have to. "Morning, Priya." Using names early makes you feel like part of the team long before you actually are.
Eat lunch with people, not at your desk. Ask "Mind if I join you?" even if it feels awkward. Lunch is where the real office friendships start, never in the meeting room.
Ask everyone what they wish they'd known in week one. People love giving advice. You learn how things really work, and every person you ask feels a little more invested in you.
Say yes to the first after-work drink. You can leave after one. Showing up early on tells people you're open, and the invitations keep coming long after your first month.
Bring something extra to the coffee machine chats. Five minutes a day of history, art or science and you'll always have a fun story when the small talk dies down.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. You'll always have a fun story when the coffee machine chat dies down.

slides.texte_overlay: Help before you're asked. Offer to take notes, fix the printer, grab the extra chairs. Small useful moments make people remember the new guy as the one who makes their day easier.
Thank people by name in front of others. "Big thanks to Marco for showing me the system." Public credit costs nothing, and it turns colleagues into allies in your very first weeks.
